topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecturer, contextualises the cancer lecture series, and outlines the learning objectives for the session.

topics.label: Etiology of Cancer and Epidemiological Patterns
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the relative contributions of intrinsic biological processes, inherited genetics, and environmental exposures to cancer risk alongside global epidemiological evidence.

topics.label: Biological, Physical, and Chemical Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine specific infectious agents, radiation, dietary toxins, and chemical mutagens that directly or metabolically cause DNA damage and initiate carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Inflammation, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic tumor promoters, chronic inflammatory microenvironments, and host developmental timing permit the outgrowth of initiated cells.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting Carcinogenicity and Assessing Risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the genomic signatures, epidemiological studies, animal models, and in vitro assays used to prove carcinogenicity and balance human exposure risks.
